input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Carvana

ownership.value: Public company (NYSE: CVNA). Controlled company under a dual-class Up-C structure: founder/CEO Ernie Garcia III and his father Ernest Garcia II (via the Garcia Parties and Carvana Group LLC units) control approximately 83% of voting rights; related-party dealings with DriveTime Automotive Group (controlled by Ernest Garcia II). No PE sponsor or change of control; 722,713,745 Class A and 380,547,355 Class B shares outstanding as of October 26, 2026.

financials.stated_by: Carvana Q3 2026 shareholder letter (Ex-99.1 to Form 8-K, filed with SEC)

financials.metric: Adjusted EBITDA, Q3 2026 (record; 10.0% margin, down from 11.3% YoY); FY2026 guidance at higher end of $2.7-3.0 billion
Net income, Q3 2026 (6.0% margin; includes $53 million loss on debt extinguishment)

financials.stated_by: Carvana condensed consolidated balance sheet (Q3 2026 shareholder letter, Ex-99.1)

financials.metric: Total debt (short-term revolving facilities $71M + current portion of long-term debt $283M + long-term debt excluding current portion $4,874M)
financials.stated_by: Carvana condensed consolidated balance sheet (Q3 2026 shareholder letter, Ex-99.1); sum of stated balance-sheet lines

financials.metric: Committed liquidity resources ($3,049M cash + $2,071M availability under short-term revolving facilities)
Total debt (senior secured notes $3,929M + senior unsecured notes $107M, etc.; principal maturities total $4,918M)
financials.stated_by: Carvana Co. FY2025 Form 10-K, debt note

debt_events.summary: Carvana announced successful upsize and pricing of a $1.66 billion Senior Secured Term Loan B Facility, priced at one-month Term SOFR + 225 bps at 99.75% of principal, maturing seven years after closing; proceeds plus cash on hand to redeem in full the 9.00% Senior Secured Notes due 2030, reducing cash interest expense by ~$45 million per year; company reported net debt/TTM Adjusted EBITDA of 1.0x.

Carvana Co. entered a Credit Agreement (Barclays Bank PLC as administrative agent) providing the $1.66 billion senior secured term loan B maturing August 14, 2033; no financial covenants; $1.0 billion of the 9.0% Cash / PIK Senior Secured Notes due 2030 redeemed August 15, 2026 and the remainder August 22, 2026.

Early redemption of Senior Secured Notes due 2030 in Q3 2026 produced a $53 million loss on debt extinguishment; nine months 2026 saw $1,841 million proceeds from long-term debt issuance and $1,774 million payments on long-term debt.
Repaid $98 million of 2025 Senior Unsecured Notes at maturity using cash on hand.
Entered a loan agreement with Citizens Bank, N.A. for up to $250 million of transportation fleet financing; $23 million outstanding at 12/31/2025.

During 2025 Carvana voluntarily redeemed $559 million principal of 2028 Senior Secured Notes for $578 million and repurchased $52 million in the open market for $55 million (net $16 million loss on debt extinguishment); as of December 31, 2025 the company was in compliance with all debt covenants.

Historical context: Fitch notes persistently negative EBITDA before 2023 and a distressed debt exchange in 2023 (the restructuring that created the 2030/2031 cash/PIK senior secured notes, some of which still paid PIK interest in 2025).

credit_ratings.summary: S&P Global Ratings upgraded Carvana Co.'s issuer credit rating to 'B' from 'B-' with a Positive outlook, citing continued performance improvement and stronger credit metrics (S&P-adjusted leverage ~5x in 2024 vs ~17.8x in 2023); senior secured raised to 'B'/'RR4', senior unsecured to 'CCC+'/'RR6'; noted Carvana is not subject to financial covenants.

S&P affirmed Carvana Co.'s issuer credit rating at 'BB-' with Positive outlook and upgraded the senior secured issue rating to 'BB' (Recovery Rating '2', ~70% recovery) from 'BB-'; senior unsecured affirmed at 'B' (recovery '6'). S&P-adjusted leverage 2.9x and FOCF/debt 13.6% at year-end 2025; liquidity adequate (sources >1.2x uses over 12 months); no financial covenants; ~$2.3 billion TRA liability recognized Q4 2025 added to S&P-adjusted debt.
Moody's Investors Service upgraded Carvana's long-term local-currency credit rating to 'B3' from 'Caa1'; outlook positive.

Fitch assigned Carvana Co. a first-time Long-Term IDR of 'BB-' with Stable Outlook; secured notes rated 'BB+'/'RR2' and unsecured notes 'BB-'/'RR4'. Ratings reflect 2025 EBITDA of $2.1 billion (~10.5% margin), expected low-2x EBITDAR leverage in 2026, offset by controlled-company status, related-party transactions and reliance on customer loan sales (56% of EBITDA).

Fitch rated Carvana's proposed ~$1.0 billion senior secured term loan B 'BB+'/'RR2' (leverage-neutral; proceeds to repay part of the $1.66 billion 9.00% senior secured notes due June 2030); Carvana IDR 'BB-'/Stable unchanged.

output.risk_rationale: Carvana's credit profile has improved dramatically: FY2025 revenue of $20.3 billion with $1,895 million net income and $2,237 million Adjusted EBITDA, $3,049 million cash plus $2,071 million revolver availability ($5,120 million committed liquidity) at 9/30/2026, no financial covenants, covenant compliance at 12/31/2025, and a stream of upgrades in the last 12 months (S&P to BB-/Positive with secured debt to BB on 2026-03-03; Moody's to B3/Positive on 2026-06-24; first-time Fitch BB-/Stable on 2026-07-30). It remains, however, a high-yield BB-category credit with ~$5.2 billion total debt, heavy reliance on loan sales/securitization (56% of 2025 EBITDA per Fitch) that would be badly hit by an ABS market disruption, compressed Q3 2026 margins (Adjusted EBITDA margin 10.0% vs 11.3%), concentrated founder control with weak governance (Fitch 'deficient' SCP adjustment), and a record of consumer payment/title complaints (Connecticut AG $1.5 million settlement, January 2025). Hence a moderate risk call: improving and well-liquified, but not investment grade and sensitive to funding-market access.

distress_signals.summary: Margin compression in Q3 2026: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3% and GAAP operating margin to 8.9% from 9.8% YoY, with Non-GAAP total GPU down $410 (company attributes ~$200/unit to elevated fuel prices and rapidly rising benchmark interest rates).

Fitch flags structural dependence on loan monetization: customer loan sales generated ~$1.2 billion of profit in 2025 (56% of EBITDA) on ~$13 billion of originations, so a securitization/loan-sale market freeze would create material liquidity needs; also notes 1H26 gross margin compression as Carvana lowered customer rates and deterioration in 2022-2023 ABS vintages.
S&P's March 2026 ABS surveillance found elevated delinquencies and losses on CRVNA 2022-P2 through 2023-P5 series, with excess spread-dependent subordinated classes lowered on some 2023 prime trusts.

Governance concentration: Fitch assesses Carvana's governance as 'deficient' (-1 notch SCP adjustment) given controlled-company status, ~83% founder voting control and related-party transactions with DriveTime; no layoffs, CFO/executive departures, auditor changes or going-concern language were found in any 2025-2026 source reviewed (CFO Mark Jenkins remained in place per the Q3 2026 shareholder letter).

payment_behaviour.summary: Connecticut Attorney General announced a $1.5 million settlement with Carvana following hundreds of consumer complaints (2021-2023) about delayed title/registration documents, delayed payments to sellers on trade-ins and untimely loan payoffs that left consumers making payments on vehicles they no longer possessed; $1 million consumer restitution fund plus $500,000 penalty ($250,000 suspended if compliant), filed in Hartford Superior Court.

In the adversary proceeding Babin v. Carvana, LLC (4:24-ap-01025, U.S. Bankruptcy Court, E.D. Ark.), a Chapter 13 Standing Trustee challenged Carvana, LLC's lien; an Agreed Order entered 9/3/2024 avoided Carvana's lien and secured claim and allowed its claim only as unsecured (case closed October 7, 2024) — an affiliate-level consumer bankruptcy matter, not a corporate payment default.
